Commentary.Commentary: Back in action! Pakistan Women require 113 runs from 31 overs according to DLS, with Muneeba Ali and Omaima Sohail at the crease, opening for them while England's skipper, Nat Sciver-Brunt, prepares to bowl the first over. Powerplay will be in effect for the first 6 overs.
... The Run Chase ...
Given that Sophie Ecclestone and Lauren Bell are missing this contest, Pakistan Women will feel they have got things going in their favor, as these conditions would have favored Bell massively.

Rameen Shamim of Pakistan Women is up for a quick chat. She says the bowlers have done a good job. Adds that the coaches gave them specific plans for different batters and they executed them well. Mentions that the outfield was faster and they were asked to put their body behind the ball. Says that the plan was to attack the stumps. Ends by saying that she has a gut feeling that the batters will do the job, as they had some intense net sessions before this game.

Pakistan Women, buoyed by their bowling unit's performance, will look to build on their momentum and chase down the revised target of 113. With their strong bowling form, they've shown they can handle pressure, and they'll aim to do the same in the run chase. Can Pakistan Women successfully navigate the adjusted target and register a much-needed win, or will England's bowlers come up with a strong response to defend their total? We shall find out on in a while.

Sana's impressive spell was the catalyst for England's collapse, and she deserves immense credit for her exceptional performance as she took 4 for 27. Sadia Iqbal also chipped in with crucial wickets, while Diana Baig and Rameen Shamim added to England's woes. The Pakistan bowlers' outstanding effort restricted England to a relatively modest total, setting the stage for a thrilling chase.

England Women's innings was reduced to 31 overs due to rain when the side was at 79 for 7 after 25 overs. Pakistan's formidable bowling unit had England reeling with Fatima Sana's masterful seam bowling, dismantling the English batting lineup. Post the break, Charlie Dean and Emma Lamb got together and stitched a 47-run stand for the 9th wicket that has helped the English side massively.

England were reeling under Pakistan's bowling attack, but Charlie Dean and Em Arlott's crucial 8th wicket partnership has given England something to play with. The duo's heroics have helped England post a competitive score of 133. Given the interruption, the target for Pakistan Women has been adjusted according to the DLS method and Pakistan Women will now be needing 113 to win from 31 overs.

She turns around for the second, and the throw from the deep is not a good one, as Sidra Nawaz fails to collect it cleanly. England Women finish on 133/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to resume! After a long, long wait, we are going to get some more cricket. Pakistan Women players are in a huddle before they take on the field. Charlie Dean and Em Arlott are the two batters for England Women. Omaima Sohail will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...

UPDATE - 2.45 pm GMT - The official word is in now, and it will be a 31-over-per-side contest. One extra over added in and England Women will have 6 more overs to bat, and then the target will be adjusted according to DLS. The restart time remains the same, and we can already see the players warming up. Don't go anywhere as we are not far away from the action.

UPDATE -  2.32 pm GMT - The umpires, along with the match officials, are out there for a pitch inspection. They are having a close look at it, and it looks like they are happy with it. The Super Soppers are also in action, and all the covers have been removed. As we have seen throughout this tournament, the ground staff are doing a brilliant job to prepare the outfield so that we don't have any further delay. A bit of a concern about the damp patches around the boundary ropes, but that should be sorted out soon. Hopefully, the rain now stay away for the rest of this game.

UPDATE -  2.14 pm GMT - Good news, folks! It is not raining anymore, and the ground staff are in action. The covers are off from the pitch and the match officials are in some discussion as well. Oh..wow! We have a RESTART TIME as well - 3 pm GMT. Also, it will be a 30-over per-side affair.

Pakistan Women will feel hard done by. They had Australia on the ropes, but allowed things to slip by. Here, they have England Women on the ropes, but seems like the weather gods are in the mood for a second successive washout in Colombo. Usually it does rain quite a lot in Sri Lanka but particularly even more so at this time of the year, with the NorthEast monsoon making its presence felt. At such a time, holding a prestigious event such as a World Cup is always dicy and both, the hosts and Pakistan have had to face the brunt of this scheduling. A washout tonight does give Pakistan their opening points in this tournament but will most likely knock them out unofficially. They will need plenty to go their way if they have to keep their hopes alive of making it to the semis.

UPDATE - 1.32 pm GMT - The rain is pretty steady here in Colombo, and the few spectators who came to watch this game and slowly heading out as well. However, even though we are still a long way from the cut-off time for a 20-over game, it is highly likely that if and when we do resume, we will be seeing Pakistan Women chasing a revised target.

UPDATE - 12.45 pm GMT - It seems that the rain has eased off but not completely stopped. We have already started to lose overs in this contest and the cut-off time for a 20-over contest is 4.08 pm GMT.

Pakistan Women have been in this exact situation against Australia, where they had them 76/7. However, they could not finish the job, with Beth Mooney's century proving to be the difference. They'll be hoping that that's not the case here, and they manage to get the three wickets quickly when play resumes.

UPDATE - 12.21 pm GMT - Nothing much to say as it is still raining and the covers remain firmly in place over the entire ground. The weather forecast suggests this trend in the next couple of hours or so, which will make the job of the ground staff even harder. The waiting game continues...

Earlier today, Pakistan Men's cricket team began their World Test Championship 2025–27 campaign in style with a commanding win over defending champions South Africa. Batting first, they put up 378 on the board, led by fluent knocks of 93 each from Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, while skipper Shan Masood and Mohammad Rizwan chipped in with fifties. Senuran Muthusamy was the pick of the South African bowlers with six wickets. In reply, the Proteas managed 269, thanks to Tony de Zorzi’s fine hundred and Ryan Rickelton’s fifty, but the spin duo of Noman Ali and Sajid Khan shared nine wickets to give Pakistan the upper hand. Despite some hiccups in the second innings, Pakistan set a target of 277, with Muthusamy bagging another five-for. Noman Ali continued his dominance with four wickets in the final innings, while Shaheen Afridi’s fiery spell, also yielding four sealed a memorable win for the hosts.

UPDATE - 11.47 am GMT - It is properly showering now here in Colombo. Any chance of an early restart looks impossible now. However, we do have an hour of buffer time before we start losing any overs. Stick with us for more news.

UPDATE - 11.19 am GMT - Uh..oh! The drizzle has picked up pace now, and the umpire has called in for the covers. The ground staff quickly runs in and covers the whole ground. We hope that this is just a passing shower and we get back into action soon. Stay tuned for further updates.

Commentary.Commentary: At the stroke of Sophia Dunkley's wicket, the umpires have called for drinks. Pakistan Women are off to a sensational start, thanks majorly to an outstanding spell from their skipper, Fatima Sana, who hit the right areas and a perfect seam to make the ball do the talking for majority of her spell and breaking the backbone of the England Women's batting line-up. With England Women at 57 for 6 after 11.3 overs, Charlie Dean walks out next to bat with England Women in deep trouble.

OUT! LBW! A brilliant review from Pakistan Women! Sadia Iqbal gets two in two overs, and the Women in Green are well on top here in Colombo. This is pushed through a bit quicker, full and on middle, Sophia Dunkley this time goes down for the sweep, but this is too full for that shot. She misses it completely and gets hit on the front pad. There is a huge shout for LBW, but the finger stays down. It looks plumb unless there is some glove or bat involved. Muneeba Ali, the stand-in skipper, takes the review after a chat with her bowler. UltraEdge confirms that it is not the case. Ball Tracking comes up and shows three reds. It's absolute delight in the Pakistan camp. England Women are reeling at 57/6!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! Before we get into the action, huge credit goes to the ground staff here. We had plenty of overnight rain, and there was a storm as well, but they have worked really hard to get the ground ready, avoiding any sort of delay.
